posts.text:
As millions prepare to travel for Thanksgiving, Americans deserve a safe and reliable aviation system. Last week’s nationwide flight ground stop, the longest since 9/11, was unacceptable.

Congress provided $14.4 billion to modernize air traffic control, yet $9.1 billion remains

Today, I was proud to speak on the House floor and vote in support of the Major Richard Star Act, which just passed the House with bipartisan support after House Democrats forced a vote through a discharge petition.

This legislation would allow nearly 60,000 combat-injured veterans to receive their full military retirement pay and disability compensation.

Our veterans have earned these benefits through their service and sacrifice. We have a responsibility to honor that service and ensure they receive what they have earned.

After consultation with retired senior military officers and former Secretaries of Defense, I voted against the effort to block impeachment proceedings. I am deeply disappointed that House Republicans chose to shield Secretary Hegseth from accountability rather than allow Congress to consider these serious allegations. Our Constitution is not optional, and those entrusted with our national security must be held accountable when they abuse that trust.  

No Secretary of Defense, nor any cabinet member, is above the law, and no President has the authority to drag our nation into an endless war without accountability to the American people. 

For months, Secretary Pete Hegseth has helped carry out a war in Iran without congressional authorization, disregarding the constitutional authority of Congress and the limits established by the War Powers Resolution. The articles of impeachment also raise serious allegations of unlawful military strikes, extrajudicial killings, disregard for civilian lives, suppressing free speech of veterans, and abuse of power. 

Our service members have been put in harm’s way, American families are paying the price of this war, and the Secretary continues to evade accountability for his decisions. 

As a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, I take seriously our responsibility to defend the Constitution and ensure that decisions of war and peace are subject to the rule of law. Supporting our troops does not mean giving this Administration a blank check to wage war.

https://t.co/XxpTCd27Ku

posts.text:
Happy 251st Birthday to the United States Marine Corps! 🇺🇸

For 251 years, generations of Marines have answered the call to serve our nation with courage, honor, and unwavering dedication.

Today, we recognize the brave men and women of the Marine Corps, especially those from our San Joaquin Valley, for their service and sacrifice in defending our freedoms.

Semper Fi!

Today, I led a bipartisan, bicameral coalition calling on Secretary Hegseth and OMB Director Vought to expedite the delivery of $400 million in security assistance Congress provided for Ukraine, following months of unnecessary delays by the Trump Administration.

As Ukraine https://t.co/xWsWa9neVl

We must call Putin out for what he is: a war criminal. The recent Russian strikes on a school in Komyshuvakha, where 40 individuals were killed and 30 remain missing, are yet another reminder of Putin’s blatant disregard for, and direct targeting of, innocent human lives.

This is about good versus evil. We must continue to stand with the brave Ukrainian people against Putin’s depravity and indiscriminate aggression. We will hold Russia accountable.

https://t.co/O1qeaRJ5bY
The American public has spoken overwhelmingly, in both blue and red states, against chaos, corruption, and cruelty. https://t.co/xNLkVVpcp4

Happy Election Day! 🗳️

Our elections give every American the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Today, I encourage everyone across the San Joaquin Valley and our country to head to the polls and exercise their right to vote.

Your vote matters!

https://t.co/xYqHJQET1e https://t.co/Ms7k2Yz4ZW

Mr. Deputy Secretary, let's get the facts straight.

Your post claims a 20% DEFAULT rate. Your own signed letter says 20% were DELINQUENT. Being behind on a mortgage payment is NOT the same as defaulting. That's a big difference.

With home prices, groceries, and everyday bills already stretching hardworking families thin, they deserve help, not misleading claims.

President Trump proposed ZERO funding for rural home loans. Republicans and Democrats in Congress rejected that and provided $1 billion.

Yet your USDA made just 2,115 loans and let nearly $180 MILLION in funding expire. That's money that could have helped hundreds more families buy their first home.

And blaming the Republican driven shutdown doesn't add up. During Trump's first term, USDA made over 6,000 loans despite a 35-day shutdown.

Our bipartisan letter asked whether your new rules made it harder for families to qualify. We still don't have answers. 

The hope of the bipartisan members who signed this letter is to find pathways to maximize the opportunity for rural Americans to achieve first-time homeownership. As opposed to pointing fingers, let’s sit down to discuss making the dream of American homeownership a reality.

This month, I had the pleasure of joining Valentino’s Pizzeria & Italian Restaurant in Reedley for their ribbon-cutting ceremony. 

It was great to celebrate this exciting milestone with the community and present a congressional certificate in recognition of their accomplishment. 

Small businesses are the backbone of our local economy, and when they thrive, our Valley thrives.

This #MilitaryFamilyAppreciationMonth, we honor the families across the San Joaquin Valley and our nation who stand behind our service members. 

Their strength, sacrifice, and unwavering support are an essential part of our nation's service. Thank you to all our Valley military families for your dedication and commitment to our country.

Happy Halloween, San Joaquin Valley. 🎃 

Tonight, families across our Valley will come together for an evening of costumes, trick-or-treating, and Halloween fun. 

As you head out to celebrate, remember to stay alert, watch for traffic, and help keep our young trick-or-treaters https://t.co/g2D6VOuhfD

When our students succeed, America succeeds. 

I saw that firsthand at Woodlake Community Day School, where students are gaining valuable skills and building brighter futures through hands-on agricultural learning at the school’s 55-acre farm.

It was a pleasure meeting these hardworking students and dedicated staff. Congratulations to the entire school community on being named one of California’s nine 2025 Model Community Day Schools.

Trick or treat? With the President’s reckless tariffs and war in Iran, it’s all trick. 
 
Halloween candy is up 15% this year. That’s four times overall inflation. https://t.co/tGPIN4N4hw

California, Election Day is just 5 days away!

If you plan to vote in person, know your rights before you go. Every eligible voter has the right to cast their ballot free from intimidation or interference. https://t.co/oF2OOtpMjz

On #NationalFirstRespondersDay, we recognize the brave men and women who put themselves in harm’s way to keep our communities safe. 

From our firefighters and law enforcement officers to our EMTs, paramedics, and dispatchers, first responders across the San Joaquin Valley answer https://t.co/P3UrJdbh9I

Dolores Huerta dedicated her life to the people who help feed our nation. When few others would, she stood with farmworkers in the San Joaquin Valley.  
 
Because of her tireless advocacy, farmworkers secured better wages and safer working conditions, along with numerous protections they deserved. Her impact reached far beyond the fields as she continued fighting for civil rights and equality for every American. 
 
Dolores made a difference, not just in the lives of farmworkers, but in the history of our nation. She showed us what people can accomplish when they work together. The fight for fair treatment and dignity for every worker continues, and it is up to us to carry that work forward. 
 
My thoughts and prayers are with her family and loved ones.

https://t.co/DkedpxyZHT

posts.text:
Thank you to the Fresno Area Hispanic Foundation for inviting me to speak at their Negociantes Unidos Breakfast.

It was an honor to provide an update on our accomplishments in the 119th Congress, address pressing issues facing our San Joaquin Valley, and answer questions https://t.co/cnaMgwbHvm

⏰ The deadline is approaching! Middle and high school students in #CA21 have until October 26 to submit their apps for the Congressional App Challenge!
 
This is a great opportunity to showcase your creativity, strengthen your coding skills, and explore the world of technology. I encourage students in California's 21st Congressional District to submit their app before the deadline!
 
Learn more: https://t.co/LSvcUEikIq

🚨Don’t miss out! 

This morning, I’ll be joining Gurdeep Shergill on his radio show to discuss important issues facing our San Joaquin Valley, including immigration, the economic challenges facing hardworking Valley families, and the importance of making your voice heard this

It was great to visit the Farmersville Senior Center and connect with community members about issues impacting families across the San Joaquin Valley.

I enjoyed sharing my family’s origin story, hearing from local residents, and discussing the issues that matter most to our communities. Thank you to everyone who joined us!

During #RedRibbonWeek, we recognize the importance of drug prevention and education in keeping our children, families, and communities safe.

By raising awareness about the dangers of drug use and encouraging healthy choices, we can help build a safer, drug-free future for our youth across the San Joaquin Valley.

It was an honor to join our Hmong community at The Fresno Center to celebrate Hmong New Year and present a Congressional Certificate of Recognition in honor of this special occasion.

Thank you to The Fresno Center for bringing our community together and helping honor the Hmong culture and traditions for future generations!

This month, I was honored to join the Fresno Chamber of Commerce in celebrating Al Solis’ retirement from the Fresno County Economic Development Corporation. 

We thank Al for his years of dedicated service and supporting businesses across the San Joaquin Valley. Wishing him all the best in his well-deserved retirement!

🇺🇸 The deadline is approaching! High school students in #CA21 have until November 6 to apply for a nomination to one of our nation's U.S. Service Academies. 
 
Each year, I have the honor of nominating outstanding young men and women from the California's 21st Congressional District who aspire to serve our country. 
 
I encourage interested students to learn more about the nomination process and submit their applications before the deadline. 
 
Learn more down below ⤵️

https://t.co/n0hP77btgJ

This week, my office received a suspicious letter containing a powdery substance. Thanks to the swift and coordinated efforts of our U.S. Postal Inspection Service, local law enforcement, and U.S. Capitol Police, my staff was safe and unharmed. 
 
While the nature of this letter is still under forensic analysis, let me be clear: any attempts to instill fear and intimidation will not deter my dedicated staff and me from working for the people of our Valley. 

No matter the circumstance, we remain committed to serving California’s 21st Congressional District. We will continue to work with law enforcement as the investigation continues.

https://t.co/oaU8FXxHvm

I joined my colleagues in leading a bipartisan letter urging President Trump to fully enforce sanctions against Russia and cut off a major source of funding for Putin’s war against Ukraine.

As the war continues, the United States must increase pressure on Putin to take negotiations seriously and work toward a lasting peace.

Read more about it below. ⤵️

https://t.co/XKesYoXg0H

I met with the San Joaquin Valley Air Pollution Control District to discuss ongoing efforts to improve air quality and protect public health across our Valley.

Clean air is essential to the health and well-being of our communities, and I’ll continue fighting for the resources needed to build a healthier San Joaquin Valley for future generations.

Our farmers, families, and communities depend on a reliable water supply, which is why I brought together federal, state, and local leaders yesterday for our second water meeting of the year to continue this important conversation. 

Building on the more than $131 million in federal funding securement for Central Valley water infrastructure projects, I’ll continue working to deliver long-term water solutions for our Valley.

Yesterday, Team Costa joined the Indigenous Peoples’ Day celebration at Fresno City Hall and presented a Congressional Certificate of Recognition in honor of the occasion.

The celebration featured cultural performances, land acknowledgments, and traditional blessings, honoring the rich history, heritage, and contributions of Indigenous peoples to our communities.

Team Costa also recognized Deborah Gilleran with a Congressional Certificate for her years of dedication to making this annual celebration possible

Yesterday, I was up bright and early for one of my favorite traditions, honoring our Valley heroes. 🇺🇸 

I was proud to help send off Central Valley Honor Flight 36 as our Valley veterans began their journey to Washington, D.C.  

These brave men and women have given so much to our country, and honoring their service is one small way to thank them for all they have done for our nation.

My thoughts are with Pope Leo XIV following his recent health diagnosis. I am encouraged to hear that his surgery was successful and wish him continued strength, comfort, and healing as he continues on his path to recovery.

May his faith continue to guide him, and may he find strength in the prayers and support of people throughout our Valley, nation, and world.

https://t.co/ly6U9efGAE
My Statement on the Reported Assault Involving an Off-Duty ICE Officer in Fresno. https://t.co/dMNpnh9b1j

Today, I joined the Nisei Farmers League, Fresno Mayor Jerry Dyer, and community leaders to address the fear and uncertainty surrounding immigration enforcement in our Valley.

Our farmworkers are not criminals. They are hardworking people who put food on America’s tables and are essential to our nation’s food security.

I’ll continue working across the aisle to advance bipartisan immigration reform that supports our hardworking farmworkers, strengthens our agricultural economy, and ensures America’s food security.

Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies are helping power America's energy future!

Today, I joined my colleagues in introducing a bipartisan resolution recognizing October 8 as National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day.

Investing in American innovation means strengthening our energy security, creating good-paying jobs, building a more reliable energy grid, and reducing emissions.

Learn more here ⤵️

https://t.co/dEnzJcyUfB

It was an honor to celebrate Leticia Campos as the new CEO of the Marjaree Mason Center.

During Domestic Violence Awareness Month, we recognize the vital work of organizations like the Marjaree Mason Center and leaders like Leticia, who ensure survivors have access to the support, services, and resources they need to heal and thrive.

As co-chair and co-founder of the Crime Survivors Caucus, I look forward to seeing the Center’s continued impact and remain committed to working alongside advocates and partners to secure the resources and support survivors deserve.

The President himself has voted by mail, yet he has repeatedly criticized the practice. Now, he is encouraging the very same voting method he has spoken out against. That is hypocrisy.

As of Monday, California counties have begun mailing ballots to registered voters for this election season. 

This is the time to make your voice heard and exercise your right to vote. Your voice matters, and your vote matters.
My statement on the third anniversary of the Hamas terrorist attack on October 7th. https://t.co/TYL1All14n

For the President of the United States to suggest allowing Iran to ‘take out’ Los Angeles and San Diego is reckless, and yet another example of his disturbing pattern of using dangerous rhetoric that incites violence. 
 
Los Angeles and San Diego are home to millions of families, workers, service members, and communities. San Diego is also home to one of the largest naval communities in the country, where thousands of service members and their families live, work, and serve. Threats of violence against our cities should never be treated as political rhetoric, especially by the President of the United States. 

This kind of language is unacceptable and has no place in our country.

https://t.co/duZUcsDg6N

Mi oficina está al tanto de los reportes sobre operativos federales de inmigración en Fresno y los condados circundantes, y estamos monitoreando de cerca la situación. He estado en contacto con funcionarios locales y federales, así como con organizaciones comunitarias, mientras trabajamos para obtener más información sobre estos reportes.

Mi prioridad es asegurar que nuestras comunidades tengan información precisa y que se protejan los derechos y la seguridad de los residentes del Valle Central. Compartiremos información adicional a medida que sepamos más.

A quienes están tan preocupados como yo, les pido que se mantengan atentos y nos ayuden a entender lo que está ocurriendo en nuestro Valle. Si presencian un operativo de inmigración en su comunidad o lugar de trabajo, o creen que durante un operativo se pudieron haber violado los derechos de alguna persona, comuníquense con mi oficina y cuéntennos lo que presenciaron. Documentar estos incidentes nos ayuda a entender lo que está sucediendo y determinar qué medidas adicionales pueden ser necesarias.

Se han planteado serias dudas sobre si las autoridades federales de inmigración están actuando de conformidad con la ley, además de incidentes que han resultado en lesiones graves y muertes, incluso de ciudadanos estadounidenses. Las autoridades federales de inmigración deben cumplir con la ley y respetar los derechos constitucionales y la seguridad de todas las personas.

En este momento, les pido a todos que conozcan sus derechos al interactuar con las autoridades federales de inmigración. Les invitamos a consultar estos recursos y compartirlos con sus familiares, amigos y miembros de la comunidad.

https://t.co/77UoNavRrE

My office is aware of reports of federal immigration enforcement activity in Fresno and surrounding counties and is closely monitoring the situation. I have been in contact with local and federal officials and key advocates as we work to gather more information about these troubling reports.

My priority is making sure our communities have accurate information and that the rights and safety of Central Valley residents are protected. We will share additional information as we learn more.

For those who are as concerned as I am, I encourage you to stay engaged and help us understand what is happening in our Valley. If you witness immigration enforcement activity in your community or workplace, or believe an enforcement action may have violated someone’s rights, please contact my office and let us know what you witnessed. Documenting these incidents helps us understand what is happening on the ground and determine where further action may be necessary.

We have seen serious questions raised about whether federal immigration enforcement actions are complying with the law, as well as incidents resulting in serious injuries and deaths, including those involving U.S. citizens. Federal immigration authorities must follow the law and respect the constitutional rights and safety of every person.

At this time, I encourage everyone to know their rights if interacting with federal immigration authorities. Please review and share the resources below with your family and community. 

https://t.co/77UoNavRrE

For 115 years, St. Mary Armenian Apostolic Church has kept Armenian faith, culture, and traditions strong in the Central Valley, serving generations of Armenian families.

It was a privilege to celebrate this historic milestone alongside His Eminence Archbishop Hovnan Derderian and present a Congressional Recognition honoring St. Mary’s enduring legacy and its important place in our Valley’s Armenian community.

Over the weekend, I had the honor of joining the California Association of Clinical Nurse Specialists Fall Conference. I was especially proud that, for the first time, the conference was hosted right here in the Central Valley.  
 
Clinical Nurse Specialists are innovators, educators, researchers, and clinical experts who improve patient outcomes, strengthen our healthcare workforce, and advance evidence-based care.  
 
I will continue working to support the nurses and healthcare professionals who care for our communities every day.

Today, on #NationalDayofNonViolence, we reaffirm the importance of peace, tolerance, and understanding in our communities. 

As we move forward, we must continue working together to create safer communities, raise awareness, and promote a culture of respect and nonviolence.

Happy birthday to Yosemite National Park! 
 
For 136 years, Yosemite has stood as one of our nation’s greatest natural treasures. I remain committed to protecting its natural, historic, and cultural landscapes so future generations can continue to enjoy all that Yosemite has to offer.

October marks #DomesticViolenceAwarenessMonth, a time to stand with survivors and recommit ourselves to building a future free from violence, fear, and abuse. 

As co-founder and co-chair of the bipartisan Crime Survivors and Justice Caucus, I remain committed to ensuring survivors have access to the support and resources they need. 

Free, confidential help is available at https://t.co/FosWnWCQTh or by calling 800-799-SAFE (7233).

I’m leading a bipartisan effort to protect $232 million in rural homeownership funding that is at risk of expiring at the end of this fiscal year.

If we don’t act now, millions of dollars intended to help rural families achieve homeownership could go unused.

I’m calling on USDA to protect these funds and make sure they reach the families they were intended to serve.

Last night, I joined small business owners, entrepreneurs, and community leaders at the Downtown Connection in Fresno. 

Small businesses are the backbone of our local economy — creating jobs, strengthening our communities, and driving economic growth. 

Thank you to the Fresno Area Hispanic Foundation and its partners for bringing our business community together to build new connections and opportunities across the region.

Interested in attending a U.S. Service Academy? 

Applications for Service Academy nominations are open! I encourage eligible high school students in California’s 21st Congressional District to explore this opportunity and apply. 

🎓 Learn more and apply today:
 https://t.co/n0hP77aVrb
